summary.intent: Make Akshat's ask-soony dashboard (with its voice 'Talk to the assistant' feature) usable from the user's phone, which requires HTTPS for microphone access and password protection since the API has no login.
summary.outcome: Added an optional basic-auth module (basic_auth.py) hooked into the dashboard, added a second tunnel hostname (ask-soony-app.stenglein.dev -> port 8000) with a DNS route, got the dashboard tests passing (12/12) with clean lint, restarted the dashboard and tunnel with auth enabled, tested the phone URL, and committed the change.

repo: The ask-soony dashboard API has no login of its own, so access protection has to be added in front of it.
Password protection reuses the same ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD env var as the user's change dashboard.
Auth was made opt-in at startup so existing tests and non-exposed runs keep working without a password.
The existing Cloudflare-style tunnel can serve multiple hostnames; a second ingress entry plus a DNS route exposes the dashboard on port 8000.

code.finding: New standalone basic-auth module that wraps Akshat's app and is hooked in with a single line; enabled only when a password is configured.

workflow: Browsers only allow microphone access on secure (HTTPS) pages, so phone voice features need a TLS-terminating tunnel rather than plain LAN access.
After adding auth, rerun tests and lint (long-line fixes were needed) before restarting services and testing the externally reachable URL.

friction: Initial auth integration broke the dashboard tests, requiring a follow-up change to make auth opt-in at startup.
Lint flagged long lines that needed a separate fix and test rerun.
open_items: Result of the external phone URL test is not stated in the transcript; confirm login and microphone work on the actual phone.
Changes were made in Akshat's project, so he may need to be told about the optional password module and commit.
Dashboard and tunnel were restarted manually; persistence across reboots is not addressed.
